{"full_contract_with_original_span_markers":"<SPAN 0>NON-DISCLOSURE AGREEMENT</SPAN 0>
<SPAN 1>THIS AGREEMENT </SPAN 1><SPAN 2>is made the ……….. day of ……………….. 2008</SPAN 2>
<SPAN 3>BETWEEN:</SPAN 3>
<SPAN 4>(1) Transnet Limited (“Transnet”) (Registration Number 1990/000900/06) whose registered office is at 49th Floor, Carlton Centre, 150 Commissioner Street, Johannesburg 2001, and</SPAN 4>
<SPAN 5>(2) […………………….] (“the Company”) (Registration Number ……………) whose registered office is at [……………………………]</SPAN 5>
<SPAN 6>WHEREAS</SPAN 6>
<SPAN 7>Transnet and the Company wish to exchange Information (as defined below) and it is envisaged that each party may from time to time receive Information relating to the other in respect thereof. </SPAN 7><SPAN 8>In consideration of each party making available to the other such Information, the parties jointly agree that any dealings between them shall be subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement which themselves will be subject to the parameters of the Proposal.</SPAN 8>
<SPAN 9>IT IS HEREBY AGREED</SPAN 9>
<SPAN 10>1. Interpretation</SPAN 10>
<SPAN 11>1.1 </SPAN 11><SPAN 12>In this Agreement:-</SPAN 12>
<SPAN 13>“Agents” means directors, officers, employees, agents, professional advisers, contractors or sub-contractors, or any Group member;</SPAN 13>
<SPAN 14>“Confidential Information” means Information relating to one party (the “Disclosing Party”) and/or the business carried on or proposed or intended to be carried on by that party and which is made available for the purposes of the Proposal to the other party (the “Receiving Party”) or its Agents by the Disclosing Party or its Agents or recorded in agreed minutes following oral disclosure and any other information otherwise made available by the Disclosing Party or its Agents to the Receiving Party or its Agents, whether before, on or after the date of this Agreement, and whether in writing or otherwise, including any information, analysis or specifications derived from, containing or reflecting such information but excluding information which:-</SPAN 14>
<SPAN 15>(i) is publicly available at the time of its disclosure or becomes publicly available (other than as result of disclosure by the Receiving Party or any of its Agents contrary to the terms of this letter); or</SPAN 15>
<SPAN 16>(ii) was lawfully in the possession of the Receiving Party or its Agents (as can be demonstrated by its written records or other reasonable evidence) free of any restriction as to its use or disclosure prior to its being so disclosed; or</SPAN 16>
<SPAN 17>(iii) following such disclosure, becomes available to the Receiving Party or its Agents (as can be demonstrated by its written records or other reasonable evidence) from a source other than the Disclosing Party or its Agents, which source is not bound by any duty of confidentiality owed, directly or indirectly, to the Disclosing Party in relation to such information;</SPAN 17>
<SPAN 18>“Group” means any subsidiary, any holding company and any subsidiary of any holding company of either party;</SPAN 18>
<SPAN 19>“Information” means all information in whatever form including, without limitation, any information relating to systems, operations, plans, intentions, market opportunities, know-how, trade secrets and business affairs whether in writing, conveyed orally or by machine-readable medium;</SPAN 19>
<SPAN 20>“Proposal” means the aggregation of Transnet’s Request for Information (RFI) and Request for Proposal (RFP).</SPAN 20>
<SPAN 21>2. Confidential Information</SPAN 21>
<SPAN 22>2.1 </SPAN 22><SPAN 23>The Receiving Party will treat and keep all Confidential Information as secret and confidential and will not, without the Disclosing Party’s written consent, directly or indirectly communicate or disclose (whether in writing or orally or in any other manner) Confidential Information to any other person other than in accordance with the terms of this Agreement.</SPAN 23>
<SPAN 24>2.2 </SPAN 24><SPAN 25>The Receiving Party will only use the Confidential Information for the sole purpose of technical and commercial discussions between the parties in relation to the Proposal or for the subsequent performance of any contract between the parties in relation to the Proposal.</SPAN 25>
<SPAN 26>2.3 Notwithstanding clause 2.1, the Receiving Party may disclose Confidential Information:</SPAN 26>
<SPAN 27>(i) To those of its Agents who strictly need to know the Confidential Information for the sole purpose set out in clause 2.2 provided that the Receiving Party shall ensure that such Agents are made aware prior to the disclosure of any part of the Confidential Information that the same is confidential and that they owe a duty of confidence to the Disclosing Party. </SPAN 27><SPAN 28>The Receiving Party shall at all times remain liable for any actions of such Agents that would constitute a breach of this Agreement; or</SPAN 28>
<SPAN 29>(ii) to the extent required by law or the rules of any applicable regulatory authority, subject to clause 2.4 below.</SPAN 29>
<SPAN 30>2.4 </SPAN 30><SPAN 31>In the event that the Receiving Party is required to disclose any Confidential Information in accordance with clause 2.3 </SPAN 31><SPAN 32>(ii) above, it shall promptly notify the Disclosing Party and co-operate with the Disclosing Party regarding the form, nature, content and purpose of such disclosure or any action which the Disclosing Party may reasonably take to challenge the validity of such requirement.</SPAN 32>
<SPAN 33>2.5 </SPAN 33><SPAN 34>In the event that any Confidential Information shall be copied, disclosed or used otherwise than as permitted under this Agreement then, upon becoming aware of the same, without prejudice to any rights or remedies of the Disclosing Party, the Receiving Party shall as soon as practicable notify the Disclosing Party of such event and if requested take such steps (including the institution of legal proceedings) as shall be necessary to remedy (if capable of remedy) the default and/or to prevent further unauthorised copying, disclosure or use.</SPAN 34>
<SPAN 35>2.6 All Confidential Information shall remain the property of the Disclosing Party and its disclosure shall not confer on the Receiving Party any rights, including intellectual property rights, over the Confidential Information whatsoever beyond those contained in this Agreement.</SPAN 35>
<SPAN 36>3. Records and return of Information</SPAN 36>
<SPAN 37>3.1 </SPAN 37><SPAN 38>The Receiving Party agrees to ensure proper and secure storage of all Information and any copies thereof to at least the same standard as the Receiving Party keeps its own Confidential Information. </SPAN 38><SPAN 39>The Receiving Party shall not make any copies or reproduce in any form any Confidential Information except for the purpose of disclosure as permitted in accordance with this Agreement.</SPAN 39>
<SPAN 40>3.2 </SPAN 40><SPAN 41>The Receiving Party shall keep a written record, to be supplied to the Disclosing Party upon request, of the Confidential Information provided and any copies made thereof and, so far as is reasonably practicable, of the location of such Confidential Information and any copies thereof.</SPAN 41>
<SPAN 42>3.3 </SPAN 42><SPAN 43>The Receiving Party shall, within seven days of receipt of a written demand from the Disclosing Party or of its ceasing to be interested in the Proposal:</SPAN 43>
<SPAN 44>(i) Return all written Confidential Information (including all copies); and</SPAN 44>
<SPAN 45>(ii) expunge or destroy any Confidential Information from any computer, word processor or other device whatsoever into which it was copied, read or programmed by the Receiving Party or on its behalf (including by any person to whom disclosure has been made as permitted under clause 2.3(i) above.</SPAN 45>
<SPAN 46>The obligations in this clause 3.3 shall not apply to the extent that (but only for so long as) it is necessary to retain copies for the purpose of providing information to any regulatory authority in accordance with clause 2.3 </SPAN 46><SPAN 47>(ii) above.</SPAN 47>
<SPAN 48>3.4 </SPAN 48><SPAN 49>The Receiving Party shall on request supply a certificate signed by a director as to its full compliance with the requirements of clause 3.3 </SPAN 49><SPAN 50>(ii) above.</SPAN 50>
<SPAN 51>4. Announcements</SPAN 51>
<SPAN 52>4.1 </SPAN 52><SPAN 53>Neither party will make or permit to be made any announcement or disclosure of its prospective interest in the Proposal without the prior written consent of the other party.</SPAN 53>
<SPAN 54>4.2 </SPAN 54><SPAN 55>Neither party shall make use of the other party’s name or any information acquired through its dealings with the other party for publicity or marketing purposes without the prior written consent of the other party.</SPAN 55>
<SPAN 56>5. Duration</SPAN 56>
<SPAN 57>The obligations of each party and its Agents under this Agreement shall [be continuing and shall survive the termination of any discussions or negotiations between the parties regarding the Proposal continue for a period of 5 (five) years.</SPAN 57>
<SPAN 58>6. Principal</SPAN 58>
<SPAN 59> </SPAN 59><SPAN 60>Each party confirms that it is acting as principal and not as nominee, agent or broker for any other person and that it will be responsible for any costs incurred by it or its advisers in considering or pursuing the Proposal and in complying with the terms of this Agreement.</SPAN 60>
<SPAN 61>7. Representations</SPAN 61>
<SPAN 62>7.1 Each party agrees that any Information made available to the Receiving Party or its Agents for the purpose of negotiations or discussions in relation to the Proposal will not form the basis of, or any representation in relation to, any contract, nor constitute an offer or invitation by the Disclosing Party.</SPAN 62>
<SPAN 63>7.2 </SPAN 63><SPAN 64>Except in the case of fraudulent misrepresentation, the Disclosing Party accepts no responsibility for nor makes any representation or warranty, express or implied, with respect to the accuracy, reliability or completeness of any Information made available to the Receiving Party or its Agents.</SPAN 64>
<SPAN 65>8. Adequacy of damages</SPAN 65>
<SPAN 66>8.1 </SPAN 66><SPAN 67>Without prejudice to any other rights or remedies of the Disclosing Party, the Receiving Party acknowledges and agrees that damages would not be an adequate remedy for any breach by it of the provisions of this Agreement and that the Disclosing Party shall be entitled to seek the remedies of injunction, specific performance and other equitable relief for any threatened or actual breach of any such provision by the Receiving Party or its Agents, and no proof of special damages shall be necessary for the enforcement of the rights under this Agreement.</SPAN 67>
<SPAN 68>8.2 </SPAN 68><SPAN 69>Nothing contained in this Agreement shall be construed as prohibiting the Disclosing Party from pursuing any other remedies available by it, either at law or in equity, for any such threatened or actual breach of this Agreement including specific performance, recovery of damages or otherwise.</SPAN 69>
<SPAN 70>9. Data Protection</SPAN 70>
<SPAN 71> </SPAN 71><SPAN 72>The Receiving Party warrants that it and its Agents have the appropriate technical and organisational measures in place against unauthorised or unlawful processing of personal data and against accidental loss or destruction of, or damage to, personal data held or processed by them.</SPAN 72>
<SPAN 73>10. General</SPAN 73>
<SPAN 74>10.1 </SPAN 74><SPAN 75>Neither party may assign the benefit of this Agreement or any interest hereunder except with the prior written consent of the other, save that Transnet may assign this Agreement at any time to any member of the Transnet Group.</SPAN 75>
<SPAN 76>10.2 </SPAN 76><SPAN 77>No failure or delay in exercising any right, power or privilege under this Agreement will operate as a waiver of it, nor will any single or partial exercise of it preclude any further exercise or the exercise of any right, power or privilege under this Agreement or otherwise.</SPAN 77>
<SPAN 78>10.3 </SPAN 78><SPAN 79>The provisions of this Agreement shall be severable in the event that any of its provisions are held by a court of competent jurisdiction or other applicable authority to be invalid, void or otherwise unenforceable, and the remaining provisions shall remain enforceable to the fullest extent permitted by law.</SPAN 79>
<SPAN 80>10.4 </SPAN 80><SPAN 81>This Agreement may only be modified by a written agreement duly signed by persons authorised on behalf of each party.</SPAN 81>
<SPAN 82>10.5 </SPAN 82><SPAN 83>Nothing in this Agreement shall constitute the creation of a partnership, joint venture or agency between the parties.</SPAN 83>
<SPAN 84>10.6 </SPAN 84><SPAN 85>This Agreement will be governed by, and construed in accordance with South African law and the parties irrevocably submit to the exclusive jurisdiction of the South African courts.</SPAN 85>
<SPAN 86>IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties hereto have caused this Agreement to be executed by their respective duly authorised representatives.</SPAN 86>

guidance.when: The source expressly makes return or destruction of protected information operative upon termination, expiration, rejection, or conclusion of the agreement, project, or contemplated relationship.
guidance.inspection: Separate the operative return or destruction duty from request-only duties, then verify that the stated trigger is an ending event and carry forward any scope limits or exceptions.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the ending-event trigger together with the operative return or destruction language; include a governing list introduction when the duty is an item.

guidance.when: The source expressly exempts identified copies or stored protected information from a return or deletion duty and permits their continued retention.
guidance.inspection: Read the general return or destruction rule with every overriding exception; identify what may remain, who or what system may hold it, its purpose, and continuing restrictions.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the retention permission and any governing exception transition, plus material limits such as archival-only access, dispute purpose, or continuing confidentiality.

guidance.when: The source expressly prohibits disclosure of the existence or occurrence of negotiations, discussions, an agreement in progress, receipt of evaluation material, or terms or status of the contemplated transaction.
guidance.inspection: Distinguish secrecy of the deal process or agreement facts from ordinary secrecy of confidential information, and preserve consent, audience, and publicity qualifications.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the prohibition's governing language and each relied-on enumerated subject; a generic nondisclosure clause alone is insufficient.

guidance.when: A source clause expressly addresses making, reproducing, automatically creating, returning, destroying, or retaining copies of protected information.
guidance.inspection: Classify the copy language by legal function: affirmative exception, automatic-copy acknowledgement, consent-conditioned prohibition, mere reference to existing copies, return duty, or retention carve-out. Do not infer creation permission from employee access or generic safeguarding.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the operative copy wording and its governing condition or exception; read adjacent retention or return language when it changes the clause's function.

guidance.when: The source expressly states that the agreement or disclosure grants, conveys, or confers no right or license in protected information or associated intellectual property.
guidance.inspection: Identify the denied grant separately from ownership, limited-purpose use, and review permissions; preserve any express narrow exception without treating it as a general license.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the operative no-rights or no-license wording and any material exception; ownership language may be retained as independent support but is not a substitute for an express grant denial.

guidance.when: The source expressly limits use of protected information to a stated agreement, transaction, evaluation, project, discussion, or business-relationship purpose, whether phrased as 'only' or as a prohibition with a necessary-purpose exception.
guidance.inspection: Treat the permitted purpose as the boundary of the restriction, not as permission for unrelated uses; capture both affirmative only-use wording and complementary other-purpose prohibitions.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the operative use limitation and the text identifying the permitted purpose; include a governing introduction when the rule is listed.

guidance.when: The source expressly permits creating copies needed for a stated purpose or acknowledges an automatic copying process and permits the resulting copies to exist.
guidance.inspection: Identify an affirmative operational exception or automatic-copy authorization. Do not treat a consent-conditioned prohibition, employee access, a reference to existing copies, or a retention-only carve-out as this condition.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the operative creation exception or the automatic-copy acknowledgement with its permission, and retain purpose, access, confidentiality, and duration limits.

guidance.when: The source expressly prohibits making copies and offers only later consent or approval as a release, with no affirmative operational copying exception or permitted automatic-copy process.
guidance.inspection: Read the whole copy clause and adjacent exceptions. A possible future waiver of a prohibition is not present permission to create copies; verify that no stated-purpose, necessity, or automatic-backup exception changes the polarity.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the operative copying prohibition and its consent or approval condition, plus adjacent language needed to show whether any affirmative exception exists.
